title: Health, Safety and Environmental (HSE) Specialist
description: The Health, Safety and Environmental (HSE) Specialist is responsible for implementing, monitoring, and continuously improving health, safety, and environmental programs for MAXAM's explosives and blasting operations at the Allied Gold mine site (Kurmuk). The position ensures compliance with company standards, client requirements, and applicable legal and regulatory obligations related to the transportation, storage, handling, and use of explosives. The incumbent serves as the primary HSE focal point between MAXAM and Allied Gold, promoting a strong safety culture, managing operational risks, supporting environmental compliance, and ensuring the safe and efficient execution of blasting activities. Key Responsibilities Implement and monitor MAXAM's Health, Safety, and Environmental (HSE) management systems at the Allied Gold project site. Ensure compliance with company policies, client (Allied Gold) requirements, and applicable legal and regulatory standards governing explosives and blasting operations. Conduct HSE inspections, audits, hazard identification, and risk assessments for explosives storage, transportation, charging, and blasting activities. Monitor and promote safe work practices, including adherence to permit-to-work systems, PPE requirements, and critical safety controls. Investigate incidents, near misses, environmental events, and blasting-related occurrences, and ensure timely implementation of corrective actions. Coordinate and deliver HSE inductions, training programs, toolbox talks, and safety awareness initiatives for employees and contractors. Monitor environmental aspects of blasting operations, including vibration, air overpressure, dust, noise, and fly rock, and ensure compliance with environmental requirements. Support emergency preparedness and response activities related to explosives, blasting operations, transport incidents, fires, and other site emergencies. Serve as the primary HSE liaison between MAXAM and Allied Gold, participating in client meetings, inspections, audits, and performance reviews. Prepare and maintain HSE reports, records, statistics, and compliance documentation, ensuring accurate and timely reporting. Promote continuous improvement and a proactive safety culture to achieve operational excellence and zero-harm objectives. Minimum Qualification Requirements Education Bachelor's Degree in one of the following: Occupational Health and Safety Environmental Health, Environmental Science, Mining Engineering, Geological Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Chemical Engineering Related discipline Experience Required Minimum 5 years of HSE experience in mining, explosives, construction, heavy industry or related sectors. Minimum 3 years of direct experience in explosives, blasting or mining contractor operations. Experience working under a contractor-client operating model. Experience interfacing with mine owner HSE teams. Experience in ISOs9001, 14001, 45001. Not required but is a plus if you have this certificates: -NEBOSH International General Certificate (IGC) -NEBOSH Diploma (often preferred for H&S Manager roles) -ISO 45001 Lead Auditor or Lead Implementer -IOSH Managing Safely (more often for supervisors than managers) -Mine rescue, emergency response, or first-aid qualifications relevant to the operation Preferred Open-pit mining experience. Experience with MMU operations and bulk explosive systems. Experience supporting large-scale gold mining operations.

title: Maaohjelmajohtaja
description: Maaohjelmajohtaja, Etiopia Etsimme kehitysyhteistyön ammattilaista maaohjelmajohtajaksi Etiopiaan. Tehtävän asemapaikka on Addis Abeba. Tehtävä on kokoaikainen ja vakituinen. Maaohjelmajohtajana vastaat Fidan Etiopian kehitysyhteistyöohjelman toteuttamisesta yhdessä hanketiimin ja paikallisen kumppanikirkon kanssa. Johdat Fidan maatoimiston työtä ja tuet kumppania toiminnan suunnittelussa, toteutuksessa, seurannassa ja raportoinnissa. Tehtäviisi kuuluvat myös vaikuttamistyö ja viestintä, viranomais- ja sidosryhmäsuhteiden hoitaminen, rahoitushakujen valmistelu sekä maaohjelman talousvastuu. Voit olla etsimämme henkilö, jos olet kehitysyhteistyön ammattilainen ja sinulla on kokemusta työskentelystä itäisessä Afrikassa. Fidan kehitysyhteistyön ja humanitaarisen avun tavoitteena on vahvistaa erityisesti lasten oikeutta koulutukseen ja hyvinvointiin. Työmme perustuu pitkäjänteisiin kumppanuuksiin ja vahvaan paikalliseen omistajuuteen. Läpileikkaavia tavoitteitamme ovat sukupuolten tasa-arvo, vammaisinkluusio sekä ympäristö- ja ilmastokestävyys. Näihin teemoihin liittyvä osaaminen tukee tehtävässä onnistumista. Etiopian maaohjelmassa koulutuksella on keskeinen rooli, joten kokemus koulutussektorilta katsotaan eduksi. Tehtävässä menestyminen edellyttää soveltuvaa korkeakoulututkintoa sekä kehityspolitiikan ja ihmisoikeusperustaisen työn tuntemusta. Aiempi kenttäkokemus kehittyvän maan toimintaympäristöstä on välttämätön. Eduksi katsotaan Fida Internationalin työn ja kumppaniverkoston tuntemus sekä kokemus ulkoministeriön ohjelmatuesta tai muista kehitysyhteistyön rahoitusmekanismeista. Tehtävässä tarvitaan erinomaista suullista ja kirjallista englannin kielen taitoa. Amharan kielen osaaminen katsotaan merkittäväksi eduksi. Lisäksi edellytämme matkustusvalmiutta, hyviä yhteistyö- ja vuorovaikutustaitoja sekä kykyä työskennellä monikulttuurisessa ympäristössä. Tehtävään voi sisältyä viestintää ja varainhankintaa Suomen helluntaiseurakuntien parissa. Siksi yhteys lähettävään seurakuntaan ja seurakunnan mahdollisuus osallistua työn taloudelliseen tukemiseen katsotaan eduksi. Työskentely Etiopiassa edellyttää sopeutumiskykyä, joustavuutta ja hyvää paineensietokykyä muuttuvissa tilanteissa. Työsuhteen ehdot määräytyvät kristillisiä järjestöjä koskevan työehtosopimuksen (KJTes) mukaisesti. Tarjoamme sinulle merkityksellisen työn, jonka kautta olet edistämässä lasten oikeuksia maailmalla aktiivisen roolin osana kansalaisjärjestön kehitysyhteistyötä sitoutuneen, osaavan ja kannustavan työyhteisön. Working closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners, IOM promotes humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It saves lives and protects people on the move, drives solutions to displacement, and facilitates pathways for regular migration, while providing services and advice to governments and migrants. IOM is committed to fostering a respectful, inclusive and supportive workplace where all employees can thrive professionally and feel valued. By creating such an environment, IOM aims to better harness the full potential of migration and strengthen its support to people on the move. IOM invites candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply and provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process when required. Learn more about IOM’s workplace culture at IOM workplace culture | International Organization for Migration Project Context and Scope The project titled, Regular Pathways for Employment: A collaborative approach between Kenya and Ethiopia for intra and inter-regional migration , aims to enhance regular labour migration pathways between Kenya, Ethiopia and Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries, promoting regional cooperation and safe migration. The project aims to facilitate the Governments of Ethiopia (GOE) and Kenya (GoK) to establish a labour migration governance and cooperation framework to address irregular migration, safeguard migrant workers' rights and strengthen regional partnerships. It also aims to contribute to the establishment of governance and cooperation frameworks for efficient and sustainable channels for regular migration to selected GCC countries. Kenya and Ethiopia are central to migration dynamics in the East and Horn of Africa region, acting as origin, transit, and destination countries influenced by economic, conflict, and environmental factors. Ethiopians often migrate to Kenya for education, work, or on transit to Southern Africa, Europe and North America, while both Ethiopians and Kenyans seek labour opportunities in GCC countries. In the process, migrants face significant challenges including exploitation, irregular migration, and limited legal protections partly due to inadequate bilateral agreements and weak institutional capacity. The Kenya–Ethiopia corridor is a strategically important economic zone linking northern Kenya and southern Ethiopia, characterized by cross-border trade, infrastructure development, mobility of labour, and emerging urban centres. Recent and planned investments in transport infrastructure, energy, logistics, agribusiness, and services are expected to significantly influence labour demand, skills requirements, and employment opportunities across the corridor. At the same time, there exists persistent challenges including high youth unemployment, informality, skills mismatches, gender disparities in labour force participation, and vulnerabilities related to climate shocks, displacement, and cross-border mobility. Addressing these challenges requires sustained collaborative efforts and coordinated actions between countries and regions to improve governance frameworks and ensure that migration pathways are safe, fair and gender responsive. The GoE is actively engaging in negotiations with countries of destination, including development of Bilateral Labour Migration Agreements (BLMAs); similar efforts are being undertaken by the GoK to increase access to decent employment for their respective migrant workers. Both countries are significant countries of origin for labour mobility to the Gulf Cooperation Council states. Despite the efforts, critical gaps persist, including absence of structured, inclusive, and gender-sensitive and responsive labour mobility frameworks between Ethiopia and Kenya as well as GCC countries. This has contributed to the proliferation of irregular migration, exploitation of migrant workers, and limited access to dignified work opportunities. The GoE has identified labor migration as a strategic priority for development as well as fostering regional integration. Discussions with GoK have been initiated in 2023 to pave the ground for possible MoU on labor migration between the two countries. The Ministry of Labour and Skills (MoLS) of the GoE with support from the International Organization for Migration (IOM) intends to commission a Labour Market Assessment (LMA) to generate evidence on existing and future labour demand and supply dynamics along the Ethiopia-Kenya corridor, to inform targeted policy dialogue, and support technical discussions to frame and realize the envisaged Ethiopia-Kenya Memorandum of Understanding (MoU/BLMA). As such, the purpose of this consultancy is to conduct a comprehensive labour market assessment to: Identify and analyze labour market dynamics, trends, and constraints in key economic sector

description: Job Description This position provides the unique opportunity of joining the team of a new international organisation, contributing to its lasting construction and influencing its future trajectory. ‍ Our Mission The OSC : The Organisation of Southern Cooperation (OSC) is an international intergovernmental organisation, founded in January 2020 by countries from across the Global South, to “contribute to the equitable, just, and prosperous social transformation of societies by promoting balanced and inclusive education, in order to attain the fundamental rights to liberty, justice, dignity, sustainability, social cohesion, and material and immaterial security for the peoples of the world”.
